comparisons.peer_summary: AMD was the first company to integrate a dedicated neural processing unit (NPU) on the same SoC as an x86 CPU for AI PCs.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD highlight the integration of Neural Processing Units (NPUs) into their client CPUs to enable AI PC capabilities in 2024. Intel disclosed that it ramped sales of the Intel Core Ultra Series 1, its 'first product with an integrated neural processing unit,' manufacturing it on the Intel 4 process. Similarly, AMD disclosed that it 'was the first company to integrate a dedicated neural processing unit (NPU) on the same SoC as an x86 CPU for AI PCs.' While both companies competed on being first with integrated NPUs for x86 AI PCs, Intel specifically noted the manufacturing node (Intel 4) for this series, whereas AMD's statement emphasized the architectural integration on the SoC as a first-mover claim.

sentences.text: ▪Client CPUs. In 2024, we ramped sales of the Intel® Core™ Ultra Series 1, our first product with an integrated neural processing unit for efficient processing of AI workload. The Intel Core Ultra Series 1, manufactured on the Intel 4 process, introduced the first AI PCs to the market. We also launched the Intel Core Ultra 200V Series, showcasing power efficiency and long-lasting battery life. The 200V Series, manufactured by an external foundry, leverages our Xe2 GPU architecture, bringing improved efficiency, second-generation ray tracing units and XMX AI acceleration to thin and light notebooks. During 2024, a significant majority of our client sales consisted of our 13th and 14th Gen Intel Core processors, manufactured on Intel 7, which allow us to serve the breadth of customer and computing needs in the client market.
AMD was the first company to integrate a dedicated neural processing unit (NPU) on the same SoC as an x86 CPU for AI PCs.

comparisons.peer_summary: AMD offers mobile Ryzen processors with leadership performance and battery life, including the 2024 release of Ryzen AI 300 Series with NPUs and Zen 5 architecture, previous generations with Zen 4/Zen 3+/Zen 2, and Ryzen Z1 Series for handheld gaming.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies detailed their 2024 mobile processor releases targeting AI and efficiency. Intel launched the Intel Core Ultra 200V Series, manufactured by an external foundry, which leverages Xe2 GPU architecture for improved efficiency and AI acceleration in thin and light notebooks. AMD released the AMD Ryzen AI 300 Series processors in 2024, featuring an NPU and its latest 'Zen 5' architecture. Both disclosures focus on the specific 2024 product lines that incorporated NPU technology and next-generation architectures (Intel's Xe2/AI acceleration vs. AMD's Zen 5) to address the AI PC market.

comparisons.peer_topic: PC Market AI Capabilities and Client SSD Portfolio Expansion
comparisons.peer_summary: Next-generation PCs require higher performance SSDs due to AI capabilities; SBU expanded its portfolio in 2024 with the 3500 NVMe SSD built on Micron G8 NAND, targeting demanding business and consumer workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron identify AI capabilities as a driver for new PC hardware requirements. Intel noted that the Intel Core Ultra Series 1 was the 'first AI PCs to the market,' highlighting the CPU's NPU. Micron corroborated the market shift by stating that 'next generation PCs contain high-performance neural processing chipsets as well as AI capabilities and require higher performance and higher average capacity SSDs than traditional PCs.' Intel's disclosure focuses on the CPU/NPU component driving the AI PC classification, while Micron's disclosure explains the storage implications (higher performance SSDs) resulting from these AI-capable chipsets.

comparisons.peer_topic: Processor architecture and AI Engine capabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm utilizes System-on-Chip architecture with heterogeneous computing, including Oryon and Kryo CPUs and Adreno GPUs, to enable high-performance, low-power computing. The Qualcomm AI Engine features dedicated hardware and the Hexagon NPU for high-performance on-device AI inference, supported by the AI Stack and AI Hub to simplify developer integration.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Qualcomm describe using System-on-Chip (SoC) architectures that integrate CPUs with dedicated NPUs to enable high-performance, low-power AI computing. Intel described the Intel Core Ultra Series 1 as having an 'integrated neural processing unit' manufactured on Intel 4. Qualcomm described its 'System-on-Chip (SoC) architecture with heterogeneous computing features, which uses our central processing unit (CPU) and different types of specialized engines (graphics processing unit (GPU) and neural processing unit (NPU)) to enable high-performance and low-power computing.' Both disclosures emphasize the integration of NPU engines within the SoC to handle AI workloads efficiently.
